pulls.title: 📝 Fix broken installation guide link
pulls.body:
## Summary `README.md` line 143 links to `tutorial/#install-fastapi`, but there is no `tutorial/` directory in the repository any more, so the link is dead. ## Problem The installation section ends with: ```markdown If you prefer to use `pip`, install `fastapi[standard]` inside a virtual environment. See the [installation guide](tutorial/#install-fastapi) for the alternative steps. ``` The tutorial sources moved to `docs/en/docs/tutorial/`, so the repository root no longer has a `tutorial/` directory. Resolving the link from the repository root lands on a path that does not exist. It is also the only relative link left in the whole README — every other documentation link is an absolute `https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/...` URL, e.g. `https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/async/#in-a-hurry` a few lines below. ## Change Point it at the published page: ```diff -See the [installation guide](tutorial/#install-fastapi) for the alternative steps. +See the [installation guide](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/#install-fastapi) for the alternative steps. ``` `README.md` is generated from `docs/en/docs/index.md` by the `generate-readme` pre-commit hook, so the fix is made in `docs/en/docs/index.md` and `README.md` was regenerated with `uv run ./scripts/docs.py generate-readme` rather than edited by hand. ## Verification - **The old target is absent.** `git ls-tree` of `master` has no top-level `tutorial/` entry; the top level is `.github`, `docs`, `docs_src`, `fastapi`, `scripts`, `tests`. - **The new target exists.** `https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/` serves `` and contains `

Install FastAPI

`, so the fragment resolves. That section is the "Install FastAPI" block, which is where the `pip` alternative steps are documented (`Using pip instead`), which is what this sentence points readers at. - **The generated file is consistent.** `uv run ./scripts/docs.py generate-readme` now prints `README.md is up to date ✅` and exits 0, so the `generate-readme` pre-commit hook will not want to rewrite anything. - Only these two files change, one line each. Not run: the Python test suite, `ruff`, and `mypy`. This is a Markdown-only change; the `ruff` pre-commit hooks are scoped to `types: [python]`, so nothing linted applies here.

pulls.title: ⬆ Bump pydantic-ai from 2.49.0 to 2.53.0
pulls.body:
Bumps [pydantic-ai](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai) from 2.49.0 to 2.53.0.
Release notes

Sourced from pydantic-ai's releases.

v2.53.0 (2026-10-01)

🛡️ Security

This release fixes one security issue in ConcurrencyLimitedModel. See the advisory for full details and affected versions.

  • GHSA-6fqq-452j-qhrp (high): a streamed request through ConcurrencyLimitedModel or limit_model_concurrency could keep its concurrency slot when the slot was released on a different task than the one that acquired it: after an early exit (the consumer stopped iterating, raised, or was cancelled), and also after fully consuming stream_text() with its default debouncing. Repeated streams could then block every request sharing the limiter. Agent-level max_concurrency and non-streaming requests are not affected. Reported by @​lche511. (#9478)

The fix also changes how limiters are shared: a model wrapper now raises UserError when it shares a limiter with the agent making the request or with an enclosing model wrapper, ConcurrencyLimiter.acquire() takes a slot on every call, even on the same task, and a custom AbstractConcurrencyLimiter must allow release() from another task.

Patched in 2.53.0. v1 is not affected.

What's Changed

⚠️ Compatibility Notes

  • Add oneOf schema support to TestModel's generated data by @​pydanty in pydantic/pydantic-ai#8783
  • Deprecate pydantic_ai_harness.step_persistence.naming by @​mpfaffenberger in pydantic/pydantic-ai#9499

🚀 Features

  • Count Google grounding web search queries in usage by @​pydanty in pydantic/pydantic-ai#8891
  • Add AbsurdDurability to the harness as a replacement for pydantic-ai-absurd by @​adtyavrdhn in pydantic/pydantic-ai#8946
  • Let AskUser defer questions to the host and time out a slow answerer by @​mpfaffenberger in pydantic/pydantic-ai#9509
  • Add SystemOneModel to run decision models such as CLM and Laya over the /v1/systemone API by @​mpfaffenberger in pydantic/pydantic-ai#8942
  • Add ToolCallJudge to assess tool calls before execution by @​DouweM in pydantic/pydantic-ai#9041
  • Send images and documents from GPT-Live tool results to the delegated backend by @​DouweM in pydantic/pydantic-ai#9048
  • Expose the message-history repair pipeline as repair_messages by @​DouweM in pydantic/pydantic-ai#8370

🐛 Bug Fixes

  • Kill the process group when a LocalWorkspaceBackend.run timeout fires during process startup by @​dsfaccini in pydantic/pydantic-ai#9358
  • Avoid invalid-escape warning floods during CodeMode analysis by @​mpfaffenberger in pydantic/pydantic-ai#9475
  • Keep the registered Memory toolset across runs so durable execution accepts it by @​mpfaffenberger in pydantic/pydantic-ai#9489
  • Keep the registered Planning toolset across runs so durable execution accepts it by @​mpfaffenberger in pydantic/pydantic-ai#9507
  • Keep planted files from escaping BubblewrapSandbox on the next launch by @​dsfaccini in pydantic/pydantic-ai#9457
  • Render non-finite eval metrics as inf/-inf/nan by @​pydanty in pydantic/pydantic-ai#8852
  • Snap gemini-3.1-flash-image thinking efforts to minimal and high on the Gemini API by @​dsfaccini in pydantic/pydantic-ai#9515
  • Raise UnexpectedModelBehavior instead of running the wrong tool when function tool calls share a tool_call_id by @​pydanty in pydantic/pydantic-ai#8782
  • Build one streamed XaiModel thinking part per output, matching the non-streamed response by @​DouweM in pydantic/pydantic-ai#9416
  • Leave image generation calls out of the OpenAIResponsesModel replay when openai_store=False by @​DouweM in pydantic/pydantic-ai#9388
  • Build the same ModelResponse from streamed and complete OpenAIChatModel and OpenRouterModel responses by @​DouweM in pydantic/pydantic-ai#9418
  • Make OpenAIResponsesModel build the same ModelResponse from a stream as from a complete response by @​DouweM in pydantic/pydantic-ai#9417
  • Make xAI push-to-talk reply only when asked: commit_audio() alone no longer triggers a reply, and create_response() is always answered by @​DouweM in pydantic/pydantic-ai#9070
  • Tolerate OpenAI realtime status, status_details and session values the SDK does not know yet by @​DouweM in pydantic/pydantic-ai#9392
  • Stop SubAgents from forcing thinking on disk agents by @​DouweM in pydantic/pydantic-ai#9384
  • Restore DynamicWorkflow reveal announcements after compaction or history loss by @​DouweM in pydantic/pydantic-ai#9371
  • Make Logfire Temporal spans replay-safe by @​DouweM in pydantic/pydantic-ai#7006
  • Allow unschemable types in the derived Temporal ActivityConfig schema by @​pydanty in pydantic/pydantic-ai#9577
  • Let GoogleRealtimeModel declare tools whose dict values are recursive models by @​dsfaccini in pydantic/pydantic-ai#9607

New Contributors

pulls.title: 🐛 Fix regression when using `str` with `Form()`
pulls.body:
## Pull Request

Discussion: Closes https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/14471

## Description

Closes https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/14471

This fixes a regression introduced in version 0.123.2. After upgrading one of my projects, endpoints suddenly started throwing `HTTP 422` responses due to empty string form values being passed. The key was definitely being passed, but because it was empty, it was being treated as if it wasn't passed at all. Fixing this would require adding `= ""` to all my string based form endpoints, which is a lot.

The long term solution is to fix the regression itself. This commit adds an explicit check for empty string values on fields which have an explicit string type. If both conditions are met, an empty string is used instead of `None`, as it was pre-regression.

## AI Disclaimer

Nope

- [x] I added tests for the change.

pulls.body:
This PR updates the SQL database tutorial example (`tutorial001_an_py310.py`) by migrating from the deprecated `@app.on_event("startup")` event handler to the modern `lifespan` context manager using `asynccontextmanager`. 

This ensures that learners copying or following the tutorial do not run into deprecation warnings in their IDEs or modern FastAPI versions.

pulls.title: 📝 Add a section on handling errors inside background tasks
pulls.body:
This picks up #14599, which the inactivity bot closed while I was away — my fault for going quiet. The
bot suggested opening a new PR, so here it is, rewritten rather than restored.

The gap: a background task that raises cannot change a response that has already been sent, and the
exception never reaches the path operation function. From the outside a failed task looks exactly like
a successful one. #2505, #2604 and #3589 all come back to that, and the tutorial does not mention it.

What changed since the earlier attempt, after reading how the rest of the docs are written:

- the example moved into `docs_src/background_tasks/tutorial003_py310.py` and is referenced with
  `{* ... *}`, so it is covered by a test like the other examples rather than being an inline block
- `/// tip` instead of `!!! tip`, which is what the other 37 files in the tutorial use
- the heading is "Handle errors in the task", matching the sentence-case style of its neighbours
- the section is shorter, and points at the existing [Caveat](#caveat) rather than repeating it

Two tests in `tests/test_tutorial/test_background_tasks/test_tutorial003.py`: the example runs, and a
task that raises still returns 200 while the error reaches the log — which is the behaviour the section
is actually describing. `5 passed` in that directory.

Happy to trim it further if it is more than you want in a tutorial page.

pulls.title: ✅ Add unit tests for is_body_allowed_for_status_code
pulls.body:
## Summary

Add direct unit test coverage for `fastapi.utils.is_body_allowed_for_status_code`.

This small helper decides, per the OpenAPI Specification's patterned fields, whether responses may carry a body. It is used by `fastapi/exception_handlers.py` and `fastapi/openapi/utils.py`, but it had no direct test coverage: the `204/205/304` (and `1XX` numeric edge) behaviour was only pinned implicitly through request-level tests.

The new file `tests/test_is_body_allowed_for_status_code.py` pins three groups of expectations:

- `None` and the patterned codes `default`, `1XX`, `2XX`, `3XX`, `4XX`, `5XX` allow a body.
- `100`, `199`, `204`, `205`, `304` (as `int` and as `str`) do **not** allow a body.
- All other regular codes (`200`, `201`, `300`, `301`, `302`, `400`, `404`, `500`, incl. string forms) allow a body.

Behaviour tested is the current implementation (comment in the source already references the OpenAPI spec); no production code is changed.

## Verification

- `uv run pytest tests/test_is_body_allowed_for_status_code.py -q` → `29 passed in 0.34s`
- `uv run ruff format --check tests/test_is_body_allowed_for_status_code.py` → `1 file already formatted`
- `uv run ruff check tests/test_is_body_allowed_for_status_code.py` → `All checks passed!`

v2.13.1

Highlights

📤 Accurate file upload lengths

Passing a file as content= now calculates Content-Length from its remaining bytes, respecting the current file position (#1214).

🔐 Reliable proxy TLS and HTTP/2 negotiation

TLS hostname overrides now apply inside HTTP proxy tunnels without affecting the proxy's own TLS connection (#1223). HTTP/2 is advertised first when enabled, and HTTP/1.1 is omitted when disabled (#1155).

🧹 Clean WebSocket shutdown

The sync WebSocket keepalive thread now exits cleanly when a ping races with connection shutdown (#1228).

httpx2

Fixed

  • Stop the sync WebSocket keepalive thread cleanly when a ping races with connection shutdown (#1228).

httpcore2

Fixed

  • Prefer HTTP/2 during TLS protocol negotiation when enabled, and stop advertising HTTP/1.1 when it is disabled (#1155).

Release notes

Sourced from sqlmodel's releases.

0.0.47

Features

  • ✨ Add direct support for PostgreSQL, MySQL, and MariaDB, include in CI tests. PR #2103 by @​tiangolo.

0.0.46

Fixes

  • 🐛 Fix timedelta arithmetic with UTC datetime fields. PR #2101 by @​tiangolo.

0.0.45

Breaking Changes

  • ✨ Use UTC datetimes by default. PR #2099 by @​tiangolo.

datetime fields now use UTCDateTime, a custom type based on DateTime(timezone=True). It requires aware datetime parameters, normalizes them to UTC, and returns aware UTC values from database reads, including on SQLite and MySQL/MariaDB. Pydantic's AwareDatetime uses the same type, while NaiveDatetime explicitly selects DateTime(timezone=False). Plain datetime validation still accepts both aware and naive values, but naive database parameters now raise an error.

Existing databases are not changed automatically. To retain naive storage, use NaiveDatetime or an explicit Field(sa_type=DateTime(timezone=False)). Explicit SQLAlchemy types retain their existing behavior. PostgreSQL needs a column migration that explicitly specifies the timezone of existing values. SQLite and MySQL/MariaDB keep their column definitions, but existing non-UTC values need a data migration before adopting the new type. Update datetime producers, query parameters, comparisons, and any database defaults to follow the new UTC convention.

Read Datetimes and Timezones: Upgrade Existing Applications before upgrading.

Updates `python-slugify` from 8.0.4 to 9.1.1
Release notes

Sourced from python-slugify's releases.

9.1.1

Bug fix in the modern algorithm. Legacy output is unchanged and remains the permanent default.

  • Modern mode only: avoid emitting a trailing separator when a hard cut truncates through repeated post-replacement delimiters, keeping the delimiter run with the next word that fits. Legacy output and public smart_truncate are unchanged (曾楚笑, #200).

Full Changelog: https://github.com/un33k/python-slugify/compare/v9.1.0...v9.1.1

🚀 Generated with Dojo ⛩️

9.1.0

Modern-algorithm improvements and fixes. Legacy output is unchanged and remains the permanent default.

  • Modern mode only: decode uppercase &#X..; hexadecimal references as HTML allows, in addition to lowercase &#x..; (Rupayon Haldar, #195).
  • Modern mode only: preserve post-replacement output when the whole slug already fits max_length, so intentional repeated/trailing delimiters are not collapsed at the length limit. Public smart_truncate is unchanged (emme1t, #193).
  • Fix add_uppercase_char to apply insertions atomically, leaving the input list unchanged if iteration fails. Built-in transliteration tables are unaffected (Cristian Ramirez, #194).
  • Modern mode only: validate argument types up front, raising TypeError for a bool/non-int max_length or a non-str separator. Legacy behavior is unchanged (Jon Bailey, #196).

Internal: the legacy pipeline is now frozen in slugify/_legacy.py with the public slugify() dispatching by algorithm; tests reorganized under tests/.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/un33k/python-slugify/compare/v9.0.0...v9.1.0

🚀 Generated with Dojo ⛩️

9.0.0

Highlights

  • Preserve legacy slug output by default while adding explicit algorithm="modern" opt-in behavior.
  • Add explicit transliteration backend and replacement-stage controls, with matching CLI options.
  • Add opt-in AnyASCII support while preserving existing dependency and backend-selection behavior.
  • Fix CLI regex-pattern forwarding and modern-mode handling for entities, iterables, separators, and delimiters.
  • Add Python 3.14 support, packaging modernization, expanded compatibility checks, and migration guidance.

See the changelog and migration guide for details.

PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/python-slugify/9.0.0/

  • Modern mode only: preserve post-replacement output when the whole slug already fits max_length, so intentional repeated/trailing delimiters are not collapsed at the length limit. Public smart_truncate is unchanged (emme1t, #193).

Release notes

Sourced from httpx2's releases.

v2.13.1

Highlights

📤 Accurate file upload lengths

Passing a file as content= now calculates Content-Length from its remaining bytes, respecting the current file position (#1214).

🔐 Reliable proxy TLS and HTTP/2 negotiation

TLS hostname overrides now apply inside HTTP proxy tunnels without affecting the proxy's own TLS connection (#1223). HTTP/2 is advertised first when enabled, and HTTP/1.1 is omitted when disabled (#1155).

🧹 Clean WebSocket shutdown

The sync WebSocket keepalive thread now exits cleanly when a ping races with connection shutdown (#1228).

httpx2

Fixed

  • Calculate Content-Length from the remaining bytes when a file is passed as content=, respecting its current position (#1214).
  • Stop the sync WebSocket keepalive thread cleanly when a ping races with connection shutdown (#1228).

httpcore2

Fixed

  • Honor the sni_hostname extension for TLS inside HTTP proxy tunnels without applying it to the proxy's TLS connection (#1223).
  • Prefer HTTP/2 during TLS protocol negotiation when enabled, and stop advertising HTTP/1.1 when it is disabled (#1155).

Full Changelog: https://github.com/pydantic/httpx2/compare/v2.13.0...v2.13.1

v2.13.0

Highlights

🔐 Reliable TLS verification controls

The CLI --no-verify flag now disables TLS certificate verification as intended, and --verify provides an explicit counterpart (pydantic/httpx2#1140, pydantic/httpx2#1186).

🧹 Safer async stream cleanup

Stopping a streamed response early no longer risks a nested async generator finalization error (pydantic/httpx2#1204).

0.0.47


Features

0.0.46


Fixes

    • 



0.0.45


Breaking Changes


    

  • ✨ Use UTC datetimes by default. PR #2099 by @​tiangolo.
    • 



datetime fields now use UTCDateTime, a custom type based on DateTime(timezone=True). It requires aware datetime parameters, normalizes them to UTC, and returns aware UTC values from database reads, including on SQLite and MySQL/MariaDB. Pydantic's AwareDatetime uses the same type, while NaiveDatetime explicitly selects DateTime(timezone=False). Plain datetime validation still accepts both aware and naive values, but naive database parameters now raise an error.


Existing databases are not changed automatically. To retain naive storage, use NaiveDatetime or an explicit Field(sa_type=DateTime(timezone=False)). Explicit SQLAlchemy types retain their existing behavior. PostgreSQL needs a column migration that explicitly specifies the timezone of existing values. SQLite and MySQL/MariaDB keep their column definitions, but existing non-UTC values need a data migration before adopting the new type. Update datetime producers, query parameters, comparisons, and any database defaults to follow the new UTC convention.


Read Datetimes and Timezones: Upgrade Existing Applications before upgrading.

Updates `ty` from 0.0.74 to 0.0.84


Release notes

Sourced from ty's releases.




0.0.84


Release Notes


Released on 2026-09-24.


This release addresses GHSA-vxvm-j4xq-q7m4, a use-after-free vulnerability during incremental type checking that can result in arbitrary code execution when analyzing a specially crafted Python project. Users who run ty on untrusted code should upgrade to 0.0.84 or newer.


Bug fixes


    

  • Fix stale diagnostics from the LSP server after toggling showSyntaxErrors (#28759)
    • 



LSP server


    

  • Complete string keys from dictionary initializers (#28820)
    • 

  • Support LSP requests against closed documents (#28595)
    • 

  • Select projects for external files using import search paths (#28594)
    • 

  • Use workspace editor settings for external files (#28639)
    • 



Performance


    

  • Avoid repeated subtyping checks for materialized recursive protocols (#28774)
    • 

  • Skip reading notebooks when discovering scripts (#28781)
    • 



Core type checking


    

  • Avoid incorrect simplification of TypeIs materializations (#28817)
    • 

  • Fix disjointness of generic class types (#28787)
    • 

  • Fix staticmethod shadowing through generic receivers and unions (#28766)
    • 

  • Infer callable signatures from bounded type variables (#28599)
    • 

  • Infer constant membership in inline list and set literals (e.g. "foo" in ["foo"] is now inferred as Literal[True]) (#28676)
    • 

  • Infer through optional generic containers in the legacy solver (#28791)
    • 

  • Preserve call narrowing during cyclic inference (#28708)
    • 

  • Preserve intersections of type guard return types (#28796)
    • 

  • Use subtyping for constraint-set implication (#28657)
    • 



Configuration


    

  • Disable invalid-legacy-positional-parameter by default (#28834)
    • 



Other changes


    

  • Only consider reachable definitions when determining whether a condition should be exempted from redundant-condition(-strict) due to the condition being defined relative to sys.version_info, sys.platform, os.name or typing.TYPE_CHECKING (#28788)

pulls.title: ⬆ Bump urllib3 from 2.7.0 to 2.8.0
pulls.body:
Bumps [urllib3](https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3) from 2.7.0 to 2.8.0.
Release notes

Sourced from urllib3's releases.

2.8.0

🚀 urllib3 is fundraising for HTTP/2 support

urllib3 is raising ~$40,000 USD to release HTTP/2 support and ensure long-term sustainable maintenance of the project. If your company or organization uses Python and would benefit from HTTP/2 support in Requests, pip, cloud SDKs, and thousands of other projects please consider contributing financially to ensure HTTP/2 support is developed sustainably and maintained for the long-haul.

Thank you for your support.

Security

Fixed the following security issues:

  • The TLS configuration for HTTPS proxies could be ignored or overridden. (High severity, GHSA-8988-9cw3-xx77)
  • HTTPResponse.stream() and read_chunked() could buffer a chunk-size line of unbounded length in memory. (High severity, GHSA-vxq7-64xx-v4gw)
  • Chunked Deflate streaming could enter an infinite loop. (Medium severity, GHSA-gh4c-6fx4-qh6g)

[!IMPORTANT] urllib3 2.8.0 fixes HTTPS proxy TLS configuration being ignored or overridden by destination settings. Configurations relying on that behavior may require changes.

Configure proxy CA certificates and client certificates in proxy_ssl_context, and proxy identity checks with proxy_assert_hostname or proxy_assert_fingerprint. Destination client certificates and identity overrides no longer apply to HTTPS forwarding proxy connections.

[!NOTE] CVE IDs had not yet been assigned to these advisories at the time of release due to a backlog at GitHub's CNA.

Deprecations & Removals

  • Deprecated using an empty collection as the Retry option allowed_methods to retry any verb. (#5044)

Features

  • Added Url.auth_decoded and Url.auth_decoded_joined convenience properties to the result of parse_url(). (#4945)
  • Added basic_auth_encoding and proxy_basic_auth_encoding parameters to urllib3.util.make_headers(). (#5092)

Bugfixes

  • Fixed response header handling to replace obsolete folded header lines (obs-fold) with spaces in accordance with RFC 9112, preventing raw CRLF sequences from appearing in header values such as Set-Cookie. (#1362)

  • Fixed usage of proxy_ssl_context with ProxyManager when use_forwarding_for_https=True. Passing ssl_context instead of proxy_ssl_context for HTTPS proxies in this configuration now emits a FutureWarning and will raise an error in v3.0. (#2577)

  • Changed behavior of the default ConnectionPool.pool initialization. LifoQueue is now resolved from the queue module after the ConnectionPool is instantiated instead of using the default cached QueueCls class property. This is done because sometimes the queue.LifoQueue is monkey-patched late in the program, such as by gevent. (#3289)

  • Raised UnrewindableBodyError instead of ValueError when retrying a request whose body had tell() but not seek(). (#3779)

  • Decoded percent-encoded SOCKS proxy credentials before authenticating with the proxy server. (#3785)

  • Fixed HTTPResponse.drain_conn() to discard unread response data in 64 KiB chunks (same as the default amt when doing HTTPResponse.stream(...)). (#5019)

  • Fixed is_ipaddress() to detect non-standard IPv4 forms accepted by socket.connect, such as hex (0x7f000001), octal (0177.0.0.1), and decimal integers (2130706433), ensuring SSL certificate verification uses the correct mode for these addresses. (#5029)

  • Fixed HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen raising a misleading FullPoolError instead of ValueError when called with an invalid timeout argument on a pool created with block=True. (#5059)

  • Fixed port-zero handling to preserve explicit :0 values instead of substituting the default ports 80 or 443 in URL parsing, pool selection, proxy configuration, connection_from_url(), and HTTP/2 request authority. (#5071, #5101)

  • Fixed a bug where PoolManager passed the assert_hostname and assert_fingerprint parameters to HTTP connection pools. (#5077)

  • Fixed HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen() and HTTP proxy forwarding to strip URL fragments from absolute request targets before sending requests. (#5079)

  • Added safeguards to the proxy tunneling code to prevent potential security issues when handling invalid characters in the proxy host and HTTP headers. This change affects users of Python 3.10, Python 3.11, and Python 3.12 when the standard library does not contain the fix; those on newer Python versions should upgrade to 3.13.14+ or 3.14.5+ to get the same security fixes. (#5091)

  • Fixed HTTPSConnection.connect() overriding ProxyConfig.ssl_context's certificate policy and proxy identity checks with the target connection's TLS settings when forwarding through an HTTPS proxy.

    HTTPSConnection no longer applies target SNI, assertions, or client credentials to forwarding proxy handshakes and continues to use its ssl_context as a fallback when an HTTPS proxy forwards an HTTP target. (#5093)

  • Fixed URL parsing to more strictly enforce RFC 3986 host syntax, rejecting invalid host input such as raw spaces and control characters, malformed percent-encodings, and percent-encoded control characters in HTTP(S) hosts and IPv6 zone identifiers, including proxy CONNECT tunnel targets. Host normalization now also follows RFC 3986 normalization rules for percent-encoded octets by decoding percent-encoded unreserved characters and uppercasing the hexadecimal digits of retained percent-encoded octets. (#5095)

... (truncated)

Changelog

Sourced from urllib3's changelog.

Security

  • HTTPResponse.stream() and read_chunked() could buffer a chunk-size line of unbounded length in memory. (High severity, GHSA-vxq7-64xx-v4gw <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/security/advisories/GHSA-vxq7-64xx-v4gw>__)
  • Chunked Deflate streaming could enter an infinite loop. (Medium severity, GHSA-gh4c-6fx4-qh6g <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/security/advisories/GHSA-gh4c-6fx4-qh6g>__)

pulls.body:
Bumps [starlette](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette) from 1.6.0 to 1.7.0.
Release notes

Sourced from starlette's releases.

Version 1.7.0

This release adds experimental OpenTelemetry tracing, HTTP QUERY support, and response trailers in TestClient. Starlette now requires AnyIO 4.

[!WARNING] OpenTelemetryMiddleware is experimental. Its API and emitted telemetry may change in minor releases without a deprecation period.

Added

  • Add experimental OpenTelemetryMiddleware for HTTP server spans, with URL exclusions and custom tracer providers #3438, #3463, and #3520.
  • Expose the matched route through scope["route"] #3438.
  • Support the QUERY HTTP method in HTTPEndpoint, CORS, and OpenAPI 3.2 schema generation #3489.
  • Capture HTTP response trailers in TestClient and expose them through response.extensions["http.response.trailers"] #3563.
  • Support partitioned cookies in SessionMiddleware #3510.
  • Add partitioned to Response.delete_cookie() on Python 3.14 and later #3376.
  • Support IPv6 hosts in TrustedHostMiddleware and TestClient #3471.
  • Support Python 3.15 #3508.

Changed

  • Require anyio>=4.0.0,<5, dropping support for AnyIO 3 #3512.
  • Raise WebSocketDisconnected, a RuntimeError subclass, for disconnected WebSocket operations #2767.
  • Accept Collection[str] in CORSMiddleware configuration annotations, including sets and frozensets #3518.

Fixed

  • Run background tasks only after the response is sent when using BaseHTTPMiddleware #3476.
  • Return 400 for invalid multipart parser input #3492.
  • Include Vary: Origin on all normal CORS responses and vary preflight responses by all request headers that affect them #3516 and #3517.

  • Ignore Range headers when FileResponse has a status other than 200, preserving its status and full body #3568.

  • Avoid deprecated AnyIO imports in TestClient and add explicit imports in WSGIMiddleware for AnyIO 4.15 compatibility #3498 and #3501.
  • Offload debug traceback rendering to a worker thread in ServerErrorMiddleware #2858.

Updates `httpx2` from 2.12.0 to 2.13.1
Release notes

Sourced from httpx2's releases.

v2.13.1

Highlights

📤 Accurate file upload lengths

Passing a file as content= now calculates Content-Length from its remaining bytes, respecting the current file position (#1214).

🔐 Reliable proxy TLS and HTTP/2 negotiation

TLS hostname overrides now apply inside HTTP proxy tunnels without affecting the proxy's own TLS connection (#1223). HTTP/2 is advertised first when enabled, and HTTP/1.1 is omitted when disabled (#1155).

🧹 Clean WebSocket shutdown

The sync WebSocket keepalive thread now exits cleanly when a ping races with connection shutdown (#1228).

httpx2

Fixed

  • Calculate Content-Length from the remaining bytes when a file is passed as content=, respecting its current position (#1214).
  • Stop the sync WebSocket keepalive thread cleanly when a ping races with connection shutdown (#1228).

0.0.45


Breaking Changes


    

  • ✨ Use UTC datetimes by default. PR #2099 by @​tiangolo.
    • 



datetime fields now use UTCDateTime, a custom type based on DateTime(timezone=True). It requires aware datetime parameters, normalizes them to UTC, and returns aware UTC values from database reads, including on SQLite and MySQL/MariaDB. Pydantic's AwareDatetime uses the same type, while NaiveDatetime explicitly selects DateTime(timezone=False). Plain datetime validation still accepts both aware and naive values, but naive database parameters now raise an error.


Existing databases are not changed automatically. To retain naive storage, use NaiveDatetime or an explicit Field(sa_type=DateTime(timezone=False)). Explicit SQLAlchemy types retain their existing behavior. PostgreSQL needs a column migration that explicitly specifies the timezone of existing values. SQLite and MySQL/MariaDB keep their column definitions, but existing non-UTC values need a data migration before adopting the new type. Update datetime producers, query parameters, comparisons, and any database defaults to follow the new UTC convention.


Read Datetimes and Timezones: Upgrade Existing Applications before upgrading.

pulls.title: 🐛 Fix stale Content-Length in 205 Reset Content responses
pulls.body:
## Summary

A path operation that uses status `205 Reset Content` and returns anything (even `None`) produces a response whose `Content-Length` header doesn't match its (empty) body. Under Uvicorn every such request fails and the client receives a truncated response.

This PR sets `Content-Length: 0` when FastAPI drops the body of a 205 response. No other status code is affected.

## Reproduction

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI

app = FastAPI()


@app.post("/reset", status_code=205)
def reset():
    return None
```

Run it with `uvicorn main:app` and send a request:

```console
$ curl -v -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/reset
< HTTP/1.1 205 Reset Content
< content-length: 4
* transfer closed with 4 bytes remaining to read
```

Uvicorn logs the following for **every** request:

```
RuntimeError: Response content shorter than Content-Length
```

The same happens when the status is set dynamically through the `Response` parameter:

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI, Response

app = FastAPI()


@app.post("/reset")
def reset(response: Response):
    response.status_code = 205
    return {"message": "Form submitted"}
```

Here the header is `content-length: 28` while the body is empty.

**Expected:** a valid 205 response with `content-length: 0` and an empty body, so the connection can be reused.

**Actual:** `content-length` is the length of the serialized return value, the body is empty, the server errors and the connection is dropped.

## Root cause

In `get_request_handler()` (`fastapi/routing.py`), the response is built first and the body is dropped afterwards for status codes that must not have one:

```python
response = actual_response_class(content, **response_args)
if not is_body_allowed_for_status_code(response.status_code):
    response.body = b""
```

By the time `response.body` is cleared, the response class has already computed `Content-Length` from the original content (e.g. `4` for `null`), so the header goes stale.

This only causes a mismatch for 205. Starlette's `Response.init_headers()` already skips `Content-Length` for status codes below 200 and for 204 and 304, so for those there is no header to go stale. 205 is the only status FastAPI treats as "no body" (`is_body_allowed_for_status_code()` returns `False` for `< 200`, 204, 205 and 304) that Starlette still adds a `Content-Length` for.

## The fix

```python
if not is_body_allowed_for_status_code(response.status_code):
    response.body = b""
    # Unlike 1xx, 204, and 304, a 205 response is still
    # delimited by Content-Length, so it has to match the
    # now empty body
    # Ref: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9112#section-6.3
    if response.status_code == 205:
        response.headers["content-length"] = "0"
```

The change runs before the headers from the `Response` parameter are appended, so it only corrects the value computed by the response class and never overrides a header set explicitly by the user.

## Why only 205 (re: #16386)

#16386 tried to fix the same bug and was closed with the concern that the change might break something else, specifically 304 responses, which may legitimately carry a `Content-Length`. This PR is scoped to address that:

- **RFC 9112 §6.3** (message body length): any response with a 1xx, 204 or 304 status is always terminated by the first empty line after the header fields, *regardless of the header fields present*. So for those, `Content-Length` doesn't affect framing, and they are left untouched.
- **205 is not in that list**, so its body length is determined by `Content-Length`. If the header says 4 and no bytes follow, the message is malformed. That's exactly the error Uvicorn reports.
- **RFC 9110 §15.3.6**: a server must not generate content in a 205 response. With `Content-Length: 0` the response is correct and the connection stays reusable.
- **RFC 9110 §8.6**: a server may send `Content-Length` in a 304 with the size of the representation that a 200 would have returned. This PR does not touch 304, and a test confirms that a `Content-Length` set by the user on a 304 is preserved.

Why `0` rather than removing the header: without `Content-Length` or `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, an HTTP/1.1 client has to read until the connection closes to know where the response ends, which breaks keep-alive. An explicit `Content-Length: 0` is the unambiguous way to frame an empty 205.

## Tests

New file `tests/test_response_code_no_body_content_length.py`:

| Test | Before the fix | After the fix |
|---|---|---|
| 205 via `status_code=205`, returning a dict | ❌ `content-length: 28` | ✅ `0` |
| 205 via `status_code=205`, returning `None` | ❌ `content-length: 4` | ✅ `0` |
| 205 set through the `Response` parameter | ❌ `content-length: 28` | ✅ `0` |
| 304 with a user-set `Content-Length: 17` | ✅ kept | ✅ kept |

Also checked:

- The existing test suite passes, including `test_response_code_no_body.py` and the tutorial tests.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `mypy` pass on the changed files.
- Manually verified with Uvicorn: the 205 response now has `content-length: 0`, no error is logged and the connection stays open.

## Scope and compatibility

- 6 lines in `fastapi/routing.py`, only on the code path where FastAPI already drops the body.
- No public API changes.
- Responses returned directly from the endpoint (a `Response` instance) are not affected, since they don't go through this path.
- Behavior only changes for 205 responses, which were broken before.

pulls.body:
Bumps [pyjwt](https://github.com/jpadilla/pyjwt) from 2.13.0 to 2.15.0.
Release notes

Sourced from pyjwt's releases.

2.15.0

See the 2.15.0 changelog for complete release details.

2.14.0

See the 2.14.0 changelog for the complete release details and related security advisories.

Changelog

Sourced from pyjwt's changelog.

v2.15.0 <https://github.com/jpadilla/pyjwt/compare/2.14.0...2.15.0>__

Security


- Wrap recursion errors from deeply nested JWT payloads in ``DecodeError``
  instead of exposing a raw ``RecursionError``.

Added



- Support Python 3.15 by @kytta in `[#1202](https://github.com/jpadilla/pyjwt/issues/1202) <https://github.com/jpadilla/pyjwt/pull/1202>`__

Changed



    

  • JWKSetCache now stores the parsed PyJWKSet rather than the raw JWKS
payload, so a cache hit no longer re-parses every key. JWKSetCache.put()
accepts either form and raises PyJWKSetError for anything else. As a
result, PyJWKClient.get_jwk_set() returns the same PyJWKSet instance
for as long as it stays cached, rather than a freshly built one per call in
[#1208](https://github.com/jpadilla/pyjwt/issues/1208) <https://github.com/jpadilla/pyjwt/pull/1208>__
    • 

  • PyJWKClient.fetch_data() now raises
PyJWKClientError("The JWKS endpoint did not return a JSON object") when
the endpoint response is not a JSON object, instead of returning it for
get_jwk_set() to reject. Callers reaching the JWKS through
get_jwk_set() see the same error as before in
[#1208](https://github.com/jpadilla/pyjwt/issues/1208) <https://github.com/jpadilla/pyjwt/pull/1208>__
    • 



Fixed



- Return cached ``PyJWKSet`` values from ``PyJWKClient.get_jwk_set()`` instead
  of raising ``PyJWKClientError("The JWKS endpoint did not return a JSON
  object")``. ``JWKSetCache.put()`` documents ``PyJWKSet`` as the cached value,

pulls.title: 🐛 Ensure SSE endpoint generators and checkpoint streams are closed on client disconnect
pulls.body:
### Discussion

- Proposed and confirmed in Discussion: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/16346

---

### Description

In `fastapi/routing.py`, when handling Server-Sent Events (`EventSourceResponse`), the `_producer` task consumes `sse_aiter` and forwards events to `send_stream`.

When a client disconnects while the producer is awaiting `send_stream.send(...)`, the task group cancels the producer task. Because `sse_aiter` was never explicitly closed upon cancellation, the generator's `finally` cleanup block (e.g. database session teardown, locks, or external resources) would not run deterministically until garbage collection or loop termination.

This PR:
1. Wraps `_producer` iteration in a `try/finally` block that explicitly awaits `sse_aiter.aclose()` inside a shielded cancel scope.
2. Catches `anyio.BrokenResourceError` and `anyio.ClosedResourceError` in `_producer` and `_keepalive_inserter` so stream cancellation unwinds cleanly across both `asyncio` and `trio`.
3. Registers `sse_stream_content.aclose` on the request's `async_exit_stack` to guarantee `_sse_with_checkpoints` is closed during request teardown without leaking unexhausted async generators.
4. Adds regression test `test_sse_generator_closed_on_disconnect_while_send_blocked` to `tests/test_sse.py`.

pulls.title: 🐛 Fix 500 instead of 422 when validation errors contain non-finite floats
pulls.body:
Fixes the client-triggerable 500 reported in #16405.

When a JSON body contains a non-finite float literal (`NaN`, `Infinity`, `-Infinity`, accepted by `json.loads` by default) and the target field rejects it, a plain `int`, `FiniteFloat`, or a float with `allow_inf_nan=False`, the `RequestValidationError` payload embeds the raw invalid input (`"input": nan`). `jsonable_encoder` passes floats through verbatim, and `JSONResponse.render` serializes with `json.dumps(allow_nan=False)`, so rendering the 422 raises `ValueError: Out of range float values are not JSON compliant` and the client receives a 500.

The fix encodes non-finite floats in the validation error payload as their `repr` strings (`"nan"`, `"inf"`, `"-inf"`) using the existing `custom_encoder` support of `jsonable_encoder`, scoped to `request_validation_exception_handler` only:

- finite floats in `input` remain numbers
- normal application responses are unaffected
- nested non-finite inputs are covered, since `jsonable_encoder` applies `custom_encoder` on each recursive call

The websocket handler is intentionally not touched: it passes the encoded payload as the close `reason`, which does not go through `JSONResponse.render`, so it cannot raise this error.

Regression tests in `tests/test_nonfinite_validation_errors.py` cover `NaN`, `Infinity`, `-Infinity`, `FiniteFloat`, a nested dict input, a finite float staying numeric, and the valid-request path.

Credit: the `custom_encoder` approach was proposed by @mmaxjr in #16405.

pulls.title: ✅ Fix frontend test timeout with Starlette Git
pulls.body:
## Description

CI is currently failing with Starlette installed from Git: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/actions/runs/36474849913/job/109105915287?pr=16407

That's because of [this Starlette PR](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3523). Now, on ASGI HTTP spec versions < 2.4, Starlette repeatedly calls `receive()` to check for client disconnects while sending a file.

The implementation of `receive()` in the failing test doesn't include any `await`, so it never yields control to other tasks. That prevents the file-sending task from running and causes the test to time out.

https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/a3d205bf19640528718cb4f05ab77f4dfca6ad9a/tests/test_frontend.py#L580-L585

To solve this, we need to update `receive()` so it yields control. But for this particular test, we don't actually need to return anything. So, Codex suggests using `await anyio.sleep_forever()` to simulate a client waiting for the response. Starlette cancels the wait when the response finishes.

## AI Disclaimer

pulls.title: Use an explicit response_model as the item type on streaming endpoints
pulls.body:
Discussed in https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/16382.

On a streaming (generator) endpoint, `response_model` is only turned into a per-item field when it is left to the return annotation. Passing it explicitly silently disables both validation and the `response_model_*` options, and leaves the OpenAPI `itemSchema` empty:

```python
class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    secret: str

@app.get("/stream", response_model=Item, response_model_exclude={"secret"})
def stream():
    yield Item(name="public", secret="private")
```

Before this change the endpoint streams `{"name": "public", "secret": "private"}`, so a field the developer asked to exclude is served to the client, and the OpenAPI response is `{"application/jsonl": {"itemSchema": {}}}`. Writing `response_model=Iterable[Item]` instead does not help: it is rejected outright as an invalid response field.

`_populate_api_route_state` resolves the stream item type only inside the `isinstance(response_model, DefaultPlaceholder)` branch. With an explicit model, `route.stream_item_type` stays `None`, `stream_item_field` is never built, and `_serialize_data` falls back to `jsonable_encoder` plus `json.dumps`, which is the path that skips validation and the exclusion options.

An explicit `response_model` on a streaming endpoint now feeds `stream_item_field` the same way the return annotation does, and both the item type and an iterable of it are accepted. Afterwards the endpoint above streams `{"name": "public"}` and its OpenAPI response carries `itemSchema: {"$ref": "#/components/schemas/Item"}`.

The new branch only applies to generator endpoints whose response class is the default placeholder (JSONL) or `EventSourceResponse` (SSE), and it keeps the existing `ServerSentEvent` exclusion, since that is a transport wrapper rather than a data model. Non-streaming endpoints, bare iterables and return-annotation streams are untouched.

## Tests

`tests/test_stream_explicit_response_model.py` covers sync and async generators, `Iterable[Item]` and `AsyncIterable[Item]`, `response_model_exclude` and `response_model_exclude_none`, SSE, per-item validation, and the OpenAPI schema, together with a non-streaming endpoint to pin that its behaviour is unchanged. On `master` the module fails at import, because `response_model=Iterable[Item]` raises `FastAPIError`.

The rest of the suite passes: 2046 passed, 12 skipped (`tests/`, excluding `benchmarks` and `test_tutorial`, which need optional extras not installed here).

pulls.title: 🐛 Prevent stale endpoint context cache entries
pulls.body:
## Problem

`_extract_endpoint_context()` caches endpoint metadata by `id(func)` without retaining or validating the function object. After an endpoint is collected, Python can reuse that id for another endpoint, causing validation errors and logs to report the wrong file, line, or function.

## Solution

Store a weak reference alongside each cached context and validate the referenced object with `is` before using a cache hit. Callable objects that do not support weak references are still handled correctly and are recomputed instead of being retained.

## Testing

- `uv run pytest -q tests/test_endpoint_context_cache.py tests/test_custom_route_class.py tests/test_custom_middleware_exception.py tests/test_callable_endpoint.py` (10 passed)
- `uv run mypy fastapi/routing.py` (passed)
- `uv run ty check fastapi/routing.py` (passed)
- `uv run bash scripts/test.sh` (3,347 passed, 18 skipped, 5 xfailed locally; the optional CLI test was unavailable because `fastapi[standard]` was not installed)
- Fork preflight run [35815878739](https://github.com/rksharma-owg/fastapi/actions/runs/35815878739) passed the full test script on Ubuntu 3.13, macOS 3.10, and Windows 3.12 for commit `914469e4cefd8085abd3020c470a8c2e022bdd16`.

Fixes #16390

pulls.title: 👷 Fix coverage badge: keep Smokeshow HTML under size limit and fail on upload errors
pulls.body:
The coverage badge in the README currently shows `coverage ??%`. The badge worker reports:

```
No status found which matched regex ^coverage, status descriptions: []
```

No `smokeshow / coverage` status has been posted on `master` since #14992 (2026-02-27). The last commits before it (e.g. 4fce9ce, 728b097) have `Coverage 100.00%`; every code commit after it has none.

## Root cause

#14992 replaced coverage's `dynamic_context = "test_function"` with pytest-cov's `--cov-context=test`. pytest-cov records one context per parametrized case **and** per phase (`|setup`, `|run`, `|teardown`), e.g.:

```
Linux-py3.13-no-deprecation|tests/test_request_params/test_cookie/test_optional_str.py::test_optional_alias_by_alias[/optional-alias]|run
```

The combined data now has ~20k contexts, and with `show_contexts = true` the generated `htmlcov` grew to **~68 MB**, over Smokeshow's 50 MB site limit. Every upload fails with:

```
ERROR! ... status=429 response=429: You've exceeded the site size limit of 52428800.
```

Since the status is only posted after a successful upload, it's never set.

This went unnoticed because the retry loop in `smokeshow.yml` ends with `sleep 1` when all 5 attempts fail, so the step exits 0 and the Smokeshow workflow is green.

## Changes

* `test.yml`: generate the HTML report with `--omit "tests/*"`. This keeps the per-test contexts for `fastapi/` and `docs_src/` (the useful part, "which test covers this line"), while dropping the per-file pages for the test files themselves. `coverage report --fail-under=100` is unchanged and still checks tests.
* `smokeshow.yml`: exit with an error if all upload attempts fail, so this kind of breakage is visible.

## Verification

Using the coverage artifacts from the latest `master` Test run (50113da):

| | HTML size | total |
|---|---|---|
| current | 68 MB | 100% |
| with `--omit "tests/*"` | 35 MB | 100% |

(For reference, disabling `show_contexts` entirely gives 41 MB; this approach keeps contexts and leaves more headroom.)

Also checked the upload loop with a stubbed command: exits `1` when every attempt fails, `0` on success.

pulls.title: 🐛 Fix endpoint context shared and mutated across requests
pulls.body:
_extract_endpoint_context() caches the context dict per endpoint function and returned the cached dict itself. The request handler (and the WebSocket handler) then set endpoint_ctx["path"] on it, mutating the shared cached object.

When the same endpoint function is used by more than one route (or the same route handles concurrent requests), the path stored in a RequestValidationError / ResponseValidationError could be overwritten by another request, so error messages and logs reported the wrong route.

Return a copy of the cached context so each request gets its own dict.

pulls.title: 🐛 Fix stale Content-Length header for 205 Reset Content responses
pulls.body:
When a path operation returns content with a status code that must not have a body (e.g. 205 set via status_code or the Response parameter), FastAPI empties response.body, but the Content-Length header was already computed by the response class from the original content. Servers like Uvicorn then fail with "Response content shorter than Content-Length".

Reset the Content-Length header to 0 when the body is dropped.

pulls.title: fix: serialize WebSocket validation errors to JSON string in close reason
pulls.body:
The default `websocket_request_validation_exception_handler` currently passes the result of `jsonable_encoder(exc.errors())` directly to `WebSocket.close()` as the `reason`.

`jsonable_encoder(exc.errors())` returns a list, while `WebSocket.close()` expects `reason` to be a `str | None`. As a result, WebSocket request-validation errors can cause the exception handler itself to fail instead of closing the connection with the intended `1008` policy-violation code.

This change serializes the validation errors with `json.dumps()` before passing them to `WebSocket.close()`. The reason is therefore a valid string containing machine-readable JSON.

A regression test was added to verify that:

- WebSocket request-validation failures close with code `1008`.
- The close reason is a string.
- The reason contains the expected validation error.
- The behavior fails with the previous implementation and passes with this fix.

The change is intentionally minimal and does not alter the validation behavior or the WebSocket close code.

pulls.title: 🐛 Fix explicit response_model ignored on streaming generator endpoints
pulls.body:
## Pull Request

<!--
Please start with a GitHub Discussion.

Once a team member asks you to open a PR, create it and link the discussion here.

Typos, grammar issues, broken links and other small docs improvements should be reported in the pinned Discussion thread "✏️ Report small docs improvements, including typos or broken links".
Please do not open a PR for these yourself.
-->

Discussion: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/16382

## Description

When specifying an explicit `response_model` (such as `response_model=Item`, `response_model=Iterator[Item]`, or `response_model=AsyncIterable[Item]`) on generator streaming endpoints (JSONL and SSE), it was ignored during response serialization and generated an empty OpenAPI `itemSchema: {}`.

### Root Cause
In `_populate_api_route_state()`, `get_stream_item_type()` was only called when `response_model` was an instance of `DefaultPlaceholder`. When an explicit `response_model` was provided:
1. `route.stream_item_type` was never populated, leaving `stream_item_field` as `None`.
2. `route.response_field` was erroneously populated instead.
3. At runtime, streaming endpoints serialize items via `stream_item_field`. Because it was `None`, serialization fell back to `jsonable_encoder()`, bypassing model validation and field filters (`response_model_include`, `response_model_exclude`, `response_model_exclude_none`).
4. OpenAPI generation emitted an empty `itemSchema: {}` because `stream_item_field` was absent.

### Fix
In `_populate_api_route_state()`:
- Check if the route is a streaming generator (`is_sse_stream` or `is_json_stream`) with an explicit `response_model`.
- Extract the item model using `get_stream_item_type(response_model) or response_model`.
- If it is not `ServerSentEvent`, assign `route.stream_item_type = stream_item`.
- Set `response_model = None` so `stream_item_field` is created for per-item serialization, validation, and OpenAPI generation.

### Tests Added
Added `tests/test_stream_response_model.py` covering:
- Async JSONL stream with explicit model and field filtering (`response_model_exclude`, `response_model_exclude_none`)
- Async JSONL stream with `response_model=AsyncIterable[Item]`
- Sync generator JSONL stream with `response_model=Iterator[Item]`
- SSE stream with explicit model and field exclusion
- SSE stream yielding `ServerSentEvent` directly
- SSE stream with explicit `response_model=ServerSentEvent`
- Non-streaming endpoints unaffected
- Validation error raised on invalid yielded chunk in async stream
- Validation error raised on invalid yielded chunk in sync stream
- Router inclusion via `app.include_router()`
- OpenAPI schema generation (`itemSchema` for JSONL and `contentSchema` for SSE)

pulls.title: Unwrap Annotated layers in get_stream_item_type for streaming return annotations
pulls.body:
### Discussion

- Proposed and confirmed in Discussion: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/16379

---

### Description

In `fastapi/dependencies/utils.py`, `get_stream_item_type(annotation)` checks if the annotation is a subclass or instance of `AsyncIterator` or `AsyncGenerator`.

However, when a route endpoint uses `Annotated[...]` in its return type annotation (e.g. `Annotated[AsyncIterator[str], ...]` or `Annotated[AsyncGenerator[str, None], ...]`), `get_stream_item_type` failed to inspect the inner stream type because `get_origin(annotation)` returns `Annotated` rather than unwrapping to the inner origin type. As a result, FastAPI fell back to non-streaming response handling.

This PR unwraps any outer/nested `Annotated` type layers using `get_args(annotation)[0]` before checking `issubclass(origin, (AsyncIterator, AsyncGenerator))`.

Bumps [anyio](https://github.com/agronholm/anyio) from 4.12.1 to 4.14.2.
Release notes

Sourced from anyio's releases.

4.14.2

  • Changed ByteReceiveStream.receive() implementations to raise a ValueError when max_bytes is not a positive integer (#1191)
  • Fixed CapacityLimiter.total_tokens rejecting float("inf") when the limiter was instantiated outside of an event loop. The adapter setter checked for infinity by identity (value is math.inf), so only the exact math.inf singleton was accepted, while every backend setter (using math.isinf()) accepts any positive infinity (#1189; PR by @​greymoth-jp).
  • Fixed to_process.run_sync() deadlocking when the worker function writes enough data to sys.stderr to fill the (undrained) pipe buffer. The worker process now redirects sys.stderr to os.devnull as well, matching the documented behavior
  • Fixed TLSStream.wrap() matching an internationalized (unicode) host name against the peer certificate using IDNA 2003 (via the standard library) instead of IDNA 2008, which could cause the host name to be matched against the wrong certificate (#1208)
  • Fixed anyio.open_process() (and run_process()) ignoring the extra_groups argument, as it mistakenly passed the value of the group argument instead (#1209)
  • Fixed CapacityLimiter.acquire_nowait() and CapacityLimiter.acquire_nowait_on_behalf_of() raising trio.WouldBlock instead of anyio.WouldBlock on the trio backend when there are no tokens available (#1218)
  • Fixed CapacityLimiter on the asyncio backend over-granting tokens (borrowed_tokens exceeding total_tokens and available_tokens going negative) when a non-blocking acquire was made in the window between a token being released and the notified waiter resuming. The freed token is now reserved for the woken waiter right away, so the non-blocking acquire correctly raises WouldBlock (#1170; PR by @​gaoflow)
  • Fixed unnecessary CPU spin when delivering cancellation from CancelScope on asyncio under certain conditions, including improper cancel scope nesting (#1111)

4.14.1

  • Fixed teardown of higher-scoped async fixtures failing on asyncio with RuntimeError: Attempted to exit cancel scope in a different task than it was entered in when an async test raise an outcome exception (e.g., pytest.skip(), pytest.xfail(), or pytest.fail()) (#1179; PR by @​EmmanuelNiyonshuti)
  • Fixed CapacityLimiter.total_tokens rejecting a value of 0 when the limiter was instantiated outside of an event loop, contradicting the documented behavior of allowing 0 total tokens (#1183; PR by @​nyxst4ck)

4.14.0

  • Added support for Python 3.15

pulls.title: ⚡️ Avoid importing pydantic.v1 in Pydantic v2-only apps
pulls.body:
Follow-up to discussion #16355.

## Problem

Registering the first route imports the whole `pydantic.v1` package, even in an app that only uses Pydantic v2:

```
app.py                         @app.get("/items")
  fastapi/routing.py             add_api_route -> get_dependant -> analyze_param
    fastapi/utils.py               annotation_is_pydantic_v1(type_)
      fastapi/_compat/shared.py      from pydantic import v1
```

Since #14609 dropped `pydantic.v1` support, both callers of this detection (`fastapi/utils.py` and `fastapi/encoders.py`) exist only to raise `PydanticV1NotSupportedError`. For a v2-only app the answer is always `False`, and the import is never used for anything else. The `encoders.py` call site can also hit it during request serialization for any object that falls through `ENCODERS_BY_TYPE`.

Cost measured on FastAPI 0.141.1 / Pydantic 2.13.5 / CPython 3.14:

| | |
|---|---|
| AWS Lambda, arm64, 512 MB, cold start | **44 ms** median of 5 |
| Local, warm bytecode, `fastapi` and `pydantic` already imported | 4.2 ms median of 5 |
| On disk | 1.2 MB |

## Change

A `pydantic.v1` model class cannot exist unless `pydantic.v1` has already been imported, so `"pydantic.v1" in sys.modules` is a necessary condition for either detection function to ever return `True`. Both `is_pydantic_v1_model_class` and `is_pydantic_v1_model_instance` now return `False` early when that key is absent, before touching the import.

Behavior is unchanged for anyone who does define a v1 model: they imported `pydantic.v1` to do so, so they still get `PydanticV1NotSupportedError` with the same message. The only way to bypass the check is deleting `sys.modules["pydantic.v1"]` after defining a model, which is not a supported pattern.

## Tests

Two tests added to `tests/test_compat.py`, both using `monkeypatch.delitem(sys.modules, "pydantic.v1", raising=False)` so they are independent of test order:

- unit: both detection functions return `False` for a v2 model and `pydantic.v1` stays out of `sys.modules`
- integration: an app with a v2 body model handles a request end to end without importing `pydantic.v1`

The existing `tests/test_pydantic_v1_error.py` still passes, covering the branch after the guard.

pulls.title: 📝 Add testing reference to the Agent Library Skill
pulls.body:
The Agent Library Skill covers dependencies, path operations, Pydantic, responses, streaming, and tooling, but has nothing on testing. This PR adds `references/testing.md`, plus a short `Testing` section and a Quick Reference entry in `SKILL.md`.

The reference covers:

* `TestClient` with regular `def` tests.
* Creating the client in a `with` block to run the `lifespan`. If you skip it, nothing errors: requests still return `200`, but they run against state the `lifespan` never set up.
* `app.dependency_overrides`: override the innermost dependency so the outer dependency's parameters are still validated, and reset the overrides in a fixture so they don't leak into later tests.
* WebSockets with `websocket_connect()`.
* Async tests: keep using `TestClient` inside `async def` tests, and use `httpx.AsyncClient` with `ASGITransport` only when the path operation has to run in the same event loop as the test.

## Two points that differ from the current docs

* `docs/en/docs/advanced/async-tests.md` says that with async tests "we can no longer use the `TestClient` inside our test functions". It does work: `TestClient` runs the app in its own event loop on a separate thread (the AnyIO blocking portal), so requests, WebSockets, and the `lifespan`, including state yielded from it, all work inside an `async def` test. The skill recommends `TestClient` there. `ASGITransport` doesn't run the `lifespan`, and calling `app.router.lifespan_context(app)` by hand runs it but doesn't pass yielded state to `request.state`.
* The skill tells agents to declare the `anyio_backend` fixture. Since AnyIO 4.12, the default fixture is parametrized over the *installed* backends, so a missing fixture no longer fails when Trio isn't installed. It does run each test twice when Trio is installed, as it is in this repo's dev dependencies. The wording matches that behavior.

## Verification

* I extracted every Python block in `references/testing.md` and the new `SKILL.md` section and ran them with pytest against FastAPI installed from this branch: Starlette 1.6.0, HTTPX 0.28.1, Pydantic 2.13.5, AnyIO 4.15.1, Python 3.10. All 8 tests pass. I ran the 7 tests from `references/testing.md` both with and without Trio installed.
* In those 7 tests, I changed only the `assert` lines (expected status codes and bodies), and all 7 failed, so none of them pass without checking anything.
* I gave one small app (a `lifespan`, a dependency that calls an external service, and a WebSocket) to agents asked to write an async test suite:
  * Without the reference, the agent handled the WebSocket by writing the raw ASGI scope and messages itself. For the `lifespan`, it used `app.router.lifespan_context(app)`, which would silently lose `lifespan` state.
  * With the reference, the agent wrote a short suite that uses `TestClient` inside `async def` tests, and it passed.
  * For a sync suite, agents already did the right thing without the reference, and still did with it.

pulls.title: 📝 Add warning for duplicate OpenAPI path converters and tests
pulls.body:
### Summary
When two routes use different Starlette path converters on the same path template (e.g. `{id:int}` and `{id:str}`), FastAPI's OpenAPI generator strips the converter suffix via `route.path_format`, causing both routes to normalize to the same key (e.g. `/items/{id}`).

The second route silently overwrites the first in the `paths` dict.

This means:
- The **runtime router** (Starlette) matches the **first** registered route
- The **OpenAPI spec** documents the **last** registered route
- Swagger UI shows a handler that **cannot be reached at runtime**

This bug was reported in Discussion #15104 and a FastAPI collaborator confirmed it should be fixed.

### Minimal repro

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI

app = FastAPI()

@app.get("/items/{item_id:str}")
def get_str(item_id: str):
    return {"id": item_id}

@app.get("/items/{item_id:int}")
def get_int(item_id: int):
    return {"id": item_id}

# Runtime executes get_str (first match)
# OpenAPI spec documents get_int (last registered) ← wrong
```

### What this PR does

- **`fastapi/openapi/utils.py`**: adds a `warnings.warn()` in `get_openapi()` when a route (or webhook) would overwrite an existing OpenAPI path+method combination, with a message that names the colliding path and methods and explains the converter mismatch cause.

- **`tests/test_openapi_path_converter_collision.py`**: regression tests covering collision detection, the no-collision case, and a case with same param name vs different param names.

- **`docs/en/docs/tutorial/path-params.md`**: adds a note under the "Order Matters" section explaining that different path converters on the same path template collapse to the same OpenAPI path, and recommends using distinct parameter names.

## Checklist
- [x] The code change is tested and all existing tests pass
- [x] Tests covering the changes have been added
- [x] Docs have been updated where relevant
- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guide](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/contributing/)

pulls.title: ✅ Fix order-dependent tests in test_dependency_contextmanager.py
pulls.body:
`tests/test_dependency_contextmanager.py` keeps a module-level `state` dict (and an `errors` list) that the app's yield dependencies mutate in place. Four tests open by asserting the pristine value, so they only pass if nothing else in the file ran first. The file passes in definition order but any other order breaks it:

```console
$ pytest tests/test_dependency_contextmanager.py::test_sync_async_state tests/test_dependency_contextmanager.py::test_async_state
```

```
def test_async_state():
>       assert state["/async"] == "asyncgen not started"
E       AssertionError: assert 'asyncgen completed' == 'asyncgen not started'

tests/test_dependency_contextmanager.py:217: AssertionError
```

pytest honors CLI order, so naming the two tests in reversed order is enough to trigger it. Running the whole file in reverse definition order fails 4 of 22 tests (`test_async_state`, `test_sync_state`, `test_async_raise_other`, `test_sync_raise_other`), and random shuffles (for example under pytest-randomly) fail 2 to 4 tests depending on the seed.

This PR resets the shared state between tests with an autouse fixture, the same pattern `tests/test_dependency_yield_except_httpexception.py` already uses for the same reason. The file now passes in definition order, reversed, and shuffled. The reset cannot change what the existing tests check: every `errors` assertion is a membership check after the test's own request, and every `state` assertion reads keys the test itself transitions.

Tests only, no library changes.

pulls.title: Fix custom_encoder ignored for fields in BaseModel in jsonable_encoder
pulls.body:
### Description

Fixes #16366.

`jsonable_encoder()` ignores `custom_encoder` when encoding types inside a Pydantic `BaseModel`. Furthermore, when a model contains a custom type with `model_config = ConfigDict(arbitrary_types_allowed=True)`, calling `jsonable_encoder(model, custom_encoder={...})` raises `PydanticSerializationError: Unable to serialize unknown type` because `obj.model_dump(mode="json")` is called before custom encoders can run, and `custom_encoder` is not passed to the recursive `jsonable_encoder()` call.

### Solution

- Use `mode="python"` when `custom_encoder` is provided (preserving `mode="json"` for the default/fast path when no `custom_encoder` is passed).
- Pass `custom_encoder=custom_encoder` to the recursive `jsonable_encoder()` call on the dumped model dictionary.
- Add regression test `test_custom_encoders_model` covering custom arbitrary types, standard types (`datetime`), and nested models.

pulls.title: Fix: Preserve injected BackgroundTasks when returning custom Response with background tasks
pulls.body:
## Description

Fixes #11215.

When `BackgroundTasks` are injected through FastAPI dependencies or path operations, they can be silently discarded when the endpoint returns a custom `Response` that already has a background task attached.

This change merges the injected background tasks with the background task already attached to the response instead of dropping the injected tasks.

The merge is applied to both relevant response-handling paths:

* `get_request_handler`
* `_FrontendRouteGroup.handle`

The regression tests cover:

* Injected tasks with a single `BackgroundTask`
* Injected tasks with a `BackgroundTasks` collection
* Reusing the same `BackgroundTasks` instance
* Dependency-only background tasks
* Dependency and endpoint background tasks together
* Responses without injected background tasks
* Injected tasks without an explicit response background
* Mixed async and sync background tasks

The tests reproduce the issue on the main branch and pass with this change.

pulls.title: fix: preserve injected background tasks with custom responses
pulls.body:
## Description

Fixes #11215.

When `BackgroundTasks` are injected through FastAPI dependencies or path operations, they can be silently discarded when the endpoint returns a custom `Response` that already has a background task attached.

This change merges the injected background tasks with the background task already attached to the response instead of dropping the injected tasks.

The merge is applied to both relevant response-handling paths:

* `get_request_handler`
* `_FrontendRouteGroup.handle`

The regression tests cover:

* Injected tasks with a single `BackgroundTask`
* Injected tasks with a `BackgroundTasks` collection
* Reusing the same `BackgroundTasks` instance
* Dependency-only background tasks
* Dependency and endpoint background tasks together
* Responses without injected background tasks
* Injected tasks without an explicit response background
* Mixed async and sync background tasks

The tests reproduce the issue on the main branch and pass with this change.

### Description
Fixes #9364.

When sending an empty form value (`""`) for sequence bytes annotations (e.g. `list[bytes]` or `Annotated[list[bytes], File()]`) from Swagger UI or other clients, `_extract_form_body` in `fastapi/dependencies/utils.py` unconditionally called `await sub_value.read()`. - Primitive string values fall back cleanly to `results.append(sub_value)`, matching the existing type annotation `results: list[bytes | str] = []` and allowing Pydantic to handle downstream validation cleanly.

  - Optional bytes list with empty form value (`data={"files": ""}`).

pulls.title: 📝 Clarify comment about SSE event terminator
pulls.body:
Closes: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/16265

## Description

The docstring of `format_sse_event` mistakenly states that each event end up with two end-of-line characters: 
https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/50113da16fec53b66b80d75e80a89296de4fa5a5/fastapi/sse.py#L210

In fact, according to the [specification](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html#parsing-an-event-stream), event can be empty (no comments and no fields) and then it will be just one empty line.
So, two end-of-line characters in the end is only true for non-empty events. First end-of-line character is actually a part of field or comment and second (empty line) is an event terminator.

## AI Disclaimer

I used AI (Codex) to investigate, but it was mostly misleading until I learned how to read the notation in the spec and figured out the solution by myself and explained my thoughts. Then Codex approved my approach.

pulls.title: fix(dependencies): preserve Query metadata for complex fields in BaseModel dependencies
pulls.body:
### Description

When a `BaseModel` dependency contains a complex field annotated with `Query()`, such as `Annotated[list[str] | None, Query()] = None`, repeated query values are not parsed into the model.

Pydantic removes the `Annotated` metadata from the generated `inspect.signature`, so FastAPI re-infers the list field as a request body parameter. A request such as `?field=foo&field=bar` therefore produces `field=None`.

### Reproduction

```python
from typing import Annotated
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, Query
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Params(BaseModel):
    field: Annotated[list[str] | None, Query()] = None

app = FastAPI()

@app.get("/")
def read(params: Annotated[Params, Depends()]):
    return params.model_dump()

response = TestClient(app).get("/?field=foo&field=bar")
assert response.json() == {"field": ["foo", "bar"]}
```

### Solution

- Resolve annotations for `BaseModel` dependency callables with `get_type_hints(..., include_extras=True)`.
- Preserve the original `Query()` metadata during dependency parameter analysis.
- Add a regression test covering repeated list-valued query parameters.

### Verification

`python -m pytest tests/test_query_cookie_header_model_extra_params.py tests/test_dependency_class.py tests/test_dependency_models.py -q`

30 passed in 0.58s.

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` both pass.

pulls.title: Fix jsonable_encoder raising an unclear UnicodeDecodeError for non-UTF-8 bytes
pulls.body:
### Summary

`jsonable_encoder(some_bytes)` currently calls `some_bytes.decode()` with no error handling. For any `bytes` value that isn't valid UTF-8 (raw binary data — hashes, encrypted blobs, protobuf, DB blob columns), this raises an unhandled `UnicodeDecodeError` straight from deep inside FastAPI's internals, with no indication of what went wrong or how to fix it — even though a working escape hatch (`custom_encoder={bytes: ...}`) already exists and just isn't discoverable from the error.

### Fix

Wrap the decode in a named `bytes_encoder()` function that re-raises as a `ValueError` (consistent with the `ValueError` `jsonable_encoder` already raises for other unencodable types) with a message that explains the problem and points at `custom_encoder` as the fix. The existing pattern of naming non-trivial encoders as top-level functions (e.g. `decimal_encoder`, `isoformat`) is followed rather than keeping an inline lambda.

### Testing

Added three tests to `tests/test_jsonable_encoder.py`:
- `test_encode_bytes_valid_utf8`: valid UTF-8 bytes still encode correctly (unchanged behavior)
- `test_encode_bytes_invalid_utf8_raises_clear_error`: invalid UTF-8 now raises `ValueError` with an actionable message
- `test_encode_bytes_invalid_utf8_with_custom_encoder`: the existing `custom_encoder` escape hatch still works and now has a regression test

Not a breaking change for the success path; the only change is the exception type/message for previously-crashing input.

pulls.title: 🐛 Support Annotated in stream return annotations for JSONL and SSE
pulls.body:
## Pull Request

Discussion: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/16337

## Description

Fixes https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/issues/16334

### Problem
Wrapping an async stream return annotation (e.g. `AsyncIterator[T]`, `AsyncIterable[T]`, or `AsyncGenerator[T, None]`) in `typing.Annotated` causes route registration to raise `FastAPIError: Invalid args for response field!` at application startup:

```python
@app.get("/stream")
async def stream() -> Annotated[AsyncIterator[Item], "metadata"]:
    yield Item(name="foo")
```

This occurs because `get_stream_item_type()` in `fastapi/dependencies/utils.py` checks whether `get_origin(annotation)` is in `_STREAM_ORIGINS`. Because the outermost origin of `Annotated[...]` is `Annotated`, `get_stream_item_type` returns `None`. FastAPI then erroneously falls back to treating the entire streaming iterator annotation as a single HTTP response model, which Pydantic cannot serialize as a field.

### Solution
Unwrap `Annotated` layers in `get_stream_item_type` before evaluating against `_STREAM_ORIGINS`:

```python
def get_stream_item_type(annotation: Any) -> Any | None:
    while get_origin(annotation) is Annotated:
        annotation = get_args(annotation)[0]
    origin = get_origin(annotation)
    if origin is not None and origin in _STREAM_ORIGINS:
        type_args = get_args(annotation)
        if type_args:
            return type_args[0]
        return Any
    return None
```

This restores complete parity between unwrapped `AsyncIterator[T]` and `Annotated[AsyncIterator[T], ...]`:
- Routes register and run successfully.
- Yielded stream items are validated against the extracted item type `T`.
- OpenAPI schema generation correctly emits `itemSchema` for both `application/jsonl` and `text/event-stream` (SSE).

### Tests
Added comprehensive test coverage in `tests/test_stream_annotated.py`:
- `test_get_stream_item_type_unwraps_annotated`: Unit tests verifying `get_stream_item_type` unwrap behavior with single and nested `Annotated` types, sync/async iterators, and non-stream types.
- `test_stream_annotated_jsonl`: End-to-end JSON Lines streaming with `Annotated[AsyncIterator[Item], "metadata"]`.
- `test_stream_nested_annotated_jsonl`: Nested `Annotated` wrappers.
- `test_stream_annotated_async_generator`: `AsyncGenerator`.
- `test_stream_annotated_sync`: Synchronous `Iterator`.
- `test_stream_annotated_sse`: Server-Sent Events with `EventSourceResponse`.
- `test_router_stream_annotated`: Streaming route included through `APIRouter`.
- `test_stream_annotated_openapi_schema`: Verifying generated OpenAPI `itemSchema` for JSONL and SSE endpoints.

All 8 new tests fail on `master` with `FastAPIError` and pass cleanly with this fix. The existing stream and SSE test suites (67 tests) pass without regression, and all `prek` pre-commit hooks pass.

## AI Disclaimer

Prompt: Diagnose issue #16334 / discussion #16337 in FastAPI regarding Annotated stream return annotations, implement the fix in get_stream_item_type, add comprehensive tests, and ensure all tests and linters pass.
